quotes.speaker: Kerry Washington
quotes.summary_phrase: Kerry Washington on the importance of filming in Los Angeles
quotes.excerpt: I'm really proud to have done more work in LA recently. It was for me a non-negotiable.
quotes.quote: It's definitely hard. I'm really proud to have done more work in LA recently. It was for me a non-negotiable on Imperfect Women. I really felt like it was important that we shoot the show in LA because it took place in LA and because of the economy here. We didn't even know at that point that the fires were going to happen. I had just finished shooting with Ben, shooting Animals in LA, and then was able to do Imperfect Women. So, there is some work here, but not enough for sure. It's hard on all the incredible artists and artisans, crew members who either are losing jobs to local crews in other places or having to leave their families for very long periods of time in order to work. It's a tough time.

quotes.speaker: Kerry Washington
quotes.summary_phrase: Kerry Washington on maintaining authenticity in political discourse
quotes.excerpt: Can we maintain authenticity and truth in politics and marriage and all these different relationships?
quotes.quote: Whatever you're able to get in, you have to keep pushing back against that because that's in some ways what Animals is about, right? It's about, can we maintain authenticity and truth in politics and marriage and all these different relationships? And having more authenticity and truth in conversations around politics is the only thing that's going to save us. Because this, there can't be this separation of like, politics is over there, it's a bunch of guys in suits on a hill that has nothing to do with us. Because the truth is, those guys in suits on the hill are making decisions that impact what we say, what we eat, how we drive, how much stuff costs, where our kids learn, our bodies. So, your willingness even to be in that friction is so important.

quotes.speaker: Kerry Washington
quotes.summary_phrase: Kerry Washington on the necessity of making room for difference
quotes.excerpt: We have to do a better job in society and culture around making room for difference.
quotes.quote: We have to do a better job in society and culture around making room for difference. I do think that's true because I think, and it's hard, because sometimes you get on your high horse or the truth is that politics are personal. So sometimes somebody says something that seems like just a political theory and you're like, but it's my body. How can you say that? It's fair. But if you stay away from it, you're just giving up your power. You're just giving over your voice.

quotes.speaker: Kerry Washington
quotes.summary_phrase: Kerry Washington on her audition process for Scandal
quotes.excerpt: I had never met Shonda before I auditioned. I had a meeting.
quotes.quote: I had never met Shonda before I auditioned. I had a meeting. By the time Scandal came around, I was at a point in my career where sometimes I auditioned for stuff and sometimes I got offered stuff. But Olivia Pope, who was originally called Olivia Price, but that name didn't clear legally, but Olivia Pope was a character that everybody wanted to play. So I knew if I wanted to do it and I did, I had to fight for it. So I went in and met with her at first before reading. And I remember getting off the elevator and the wall was covered with a huge sign that said Shondaland. And I was like, she's not a whole land? Like, I don't know how this is going to go. I felt very nervous about somebody who maybe thought my perception was like, does she think everything revolves around her? And then I met her and loved her immediately.

quotes.speaker: Kerry Washington
quotes.summary_phrase: Kerry Washington on her personal connection to the Scandal script
quotes.excerpt: I was actually working for the White House when I read the script for Scandal.
quotes.quote: I was actually working for the White House when I read the script for Scandal. I was on the President's Committee for the Arts and Humanities. I had spent so much time traveling, campaigning for the Obamas. I had been in like 15 states all over the country trying to get people to vote. And I was really engaged in that world. And so when I read the script, I felt like it had been written for me. I was like, I'm the only person who can play this role. But there were like 20 other actresses who felt the same way, which is why we all had to read for it.
